per_token_logprobs.Why does every policy-gradient loss for: The policy gradient decomposes over tokens: log p(sequence) is the sum of per-token log-probs, and each token is an action. Sequence probabilities underflow.
per_token_logprobs.What is the difference between the logit: Logits at position t predict token t + 1. Shift: logits[:, :-1] pair with tokens[:, 1:].
per_token_logprobs.Why use log_softmax instead of softmax f: log_softmax uses logsumexp internally. softmax of large logits underflows to 0 for most entries, and log(0) = -inf.
per_token_logprobs.How do you gather the realized token's l: gather(dim=-1, index=tokens.unsqueeze(-1)): the index must have the same number of dims as the logits, with size 1 in the gathered dim.
per_token_logprobs.Full vocabulary logits for a long batch: Chunk over the sequence or batch, compute log_softmax per chunk and gather immediately, or use logsumexp(logits) - logits[token].
per_token_logprobs.Summing per-token log-probs gives a sequ: Long responses get larger-magnitude sums, so the loss scale depends on length and favors short or long outputs. Normalize.
per_token_logprobs.Where do per-token log-probs computed by: Different kernels, precision and batch composition in vLLM versus the trainer. The ratio to rollout log-probs is no longer 1, which biases the importance weights.

group_relative_advantage.What problem does GRPO's group-relative: PPO needs a critic as large as the policy to estimate a baseline. GRPO uses the other samples for the same prompt as the baseline.
group_relative_advantage.Why standardize rewards within each prom: Prompts differ in difficulty. A per-group baseline compares answers to the same question rather than rewarding easy prompts.
group_relative_advantage.What happens to the advantage when every: The numerator is zero and the std is zero, so 0/0. eps turns it into 0: no signal from that group.
group_relative_advantage.How do you reshape a flat group-major re: reshape(-1, G), then mean and std over dim 1 with keepdim, then flatten back.
group_relative_advantage.Population or sample standard deviation:: The two differ by a constant factor for fixed G, so the direction per group is unchanged but the scale changes. Know which one the reference uses.
group_relative_advantage.Dividing by the group std has been criti: Low-variance groups (nearly all right or all wrong) get amplified advantages, so easy or hard prompts get outsized weight.
group_relative_advantage.What does GRPO cost you in sampling comp: Many samples per prompt (for example 8 to 64) versus one sample plus a critic. Worth it when rewards are verifiable and critic training is unstable.

rloo_advantage.What is RLOO, and what baseline does it: REINFORCE with k samples per prompt. Each sample's baseline is the mean reward of the other k - 1 samples.
rloo_advantage.Why does including a sample's own reward: The baseline would depend on the sample's own action, so the baseline term no longer has zero expected gradient.
rloo_advantage.How do you compute every leave-one-out m: The leave-one-out mean is (group sum - r_i) / (k - 1). Compute the group sum once and broadcast.
rloo_advantage.Why must the group size be at least 2, a: With k = 1 there are no others to average. With equal rewards every advantage is exactly 0.
rloo_advantage.RLOO versus GRPO: what does dividing by: The std division rescales each group to unit variance, a per-prompt learning-rate change that biases toward low-variance prompts.
rloo_advantage.RLOO versus PPO with a learned critic: s: RLOO needs several samples per prompt but no critic. It is simple and stable, with variance depending on k. A critic is cheaper per sample but can be wrong.

k3_kl_penalty.Why do RLHF and GRPO add a KL penalty to: To keep the policy near the reference: this prevents reward hacking, language drift and forgetting.
k3_kl_penalty.What are the k1, k2 and k3 KL estimators: With r = log(ref/pi): k1 = -r (unbiased, can be negative), k2 = r^2 / 2 (biased, low variance), k3 = exp(r) - r - 1 (unbiased, non-negative, low variance).
k3_kl_penalty.Why must the log-ratio be reference minu: It estimates KL(pi || ref) only when r = log ref - log pi, with samples from pi. Flipping gives an estimate of a different quantity with no such guarantees.
k3_kl_penalty.Show that exp(r) - r - 1 is never negati: f(r) = exp(r) - r - 1 has minimum 0 at r = 0 (f' = exp(r) - 1, f'' > 0). Per-token penalties are then never negative rewards in disguise.
k3_kl_penalty.Should the KL term be detached? Which pa: The policy log-prob should carry gradient; the reference log-prob is detached, since the reference is frozen.
k3_kl_penalty.KL as a reward penalty versus KL as a se: As a reward, KL is scaled by advantages and enters through the policy gradient. As a loss term, you differentiate the estimator directly, which gives a different and possibly biased gradient.
k3_kl_penalty.What happens to k3 when the policy puts: r = log(ref/pi) is large, so exp(r) explodes and so does the gradient. Clamping would hide that and bias the estimate; this exercise deliberately does not clamp, so the caller can see and handle it.

response_token_mask.In RL post-training, which tokens should: Only generated response tokens are actions. The prompt was not chosen by the policy, and padding carries no meaning.
response_token_mask.What goes wrong in training if padding t: The loss averages in zeros or garbage, gradients go to padding logits, and length-dependent scaling becomes wrong.
response_token_mask.Build the mask for a right-padded batch: positions = arange(max_len); mask = (positions >= prompt_len[:, None]) & (positions < total_len[:, None]).
response_token_mask.How would the mask change for left-padde: Positions shift: real tokens start at max_len - len. Compute offsets from the left padding length.
response_token_mask.What are the edge cases: an empty genera: An empty generation gives an all-false row. A full row has no padding. With prompt length 0 everything up to the length is response.
response_token_mask.Multi-turn agent rollouts interleave too: Tool outputs sit inside the response but were not generated, so they must be masked too. You need a per-segment mask.
response_token_mask.Where else does the same mask get reused: It is reused in the KL term, advantage broadcast, entropy and loss averaging. An off-by-one shift trains on the wrong token or leaks the prompt.

rlvr_format_reward.What is RLVR, and why do reasoning model: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards such as math answers or tests. Format rewards teach the structure (think/answer tags) so the answer can be parsed.
rlvr_format_reward.Why give partial credit instead of a str: Partial credit gives a denser signal early, when strict all-or-nothing is almost always 0.
rlvr_format_reward.Walk through how you check that each tag: Count each tag, then check the index order. One regex tends to accept duplicates, overlaps or nesting.
rlvr_format_reward.Why require the completion to end with t: Truncated generations are not complete answers. Rewarding them teaches the model to stop mid-thought or ignore the length limit.
rlvr_format_reward.What edge cases would you test: nested t: Nested think tags, a closing tag before the opening one, tags inside answer text, empty or whitespace-only answers, and text after the final tag.
rlvr_format_reward.How can a model reward-hack a format rew: The model emits perfect tags with junk inside. Keep the format weight small, gate it on correctness, or anneal it.
rlvr_format_reward.Rule-based verifiable rewards versus a l: Verifiable rewards are cheap and hard to hack but narrow. Learned RMs cover open-ended tasks but are noisy and exploitable.

reinforce_discounted_returns.What is the reward-to-go in REINFORCE, a: Reward-to-go counts only rewards after the action, since an action cannot affect past rewards. This lowers variance without bias.
reinforce_discounted_returns.What does the discount factor gamma trad: gamma < 1 favors near-term rewards and lowers variance. gamma = 1 values all future rewards equally.
reinforce_discounted_returns.How do you compute discounted returns in: Iterate t from T - 1 down to 0: G = r_t + gamma * G. Reset G to 0 when an episode boundary is crossed.
reinforce_discounted_returns.A flat rollout contains several episodes: At a done, the return from that step is just its reward (terminal included), and the next episode's accumulation starts fresh.
reinforce_discounted_returns.What should happen for the final unfinis: It is truncated: future rewards are unknown. Using the partial sum underestimates it unless you bootstrap with a value estimate.
reinforce_discounted_returns.Monte Carlo returns versus bootstrapped: MC is unbiased with high variance. TD bootstraps from a critic: lower variance, biased by critic error.
reinforce_discounted_returns.For LLM RL with a single terminal reward: With a terminal-only reward, gamma < 1 shrinks the signal for early tokens, which implicitly favors shorter responses. Most LLM RL uses gamma = 1.

reinforce_policy_loss.Derive the REINFORCE policy gradient in: The gradient of expected return is E[return times grad log pi(a|s)], by the log-derivative trick. Sampling gives an unbiased estimate.
reinforce_policy_loss.Why does subtracting a baseline reduce v: E[b * grad log pi] = b * grad of sum pi = b * grad 1 = 0, as long as b does not depend on the action. It removes common variance.
reinforce_policy_loss.Why must returns and the baseline be det: They are weights, not things to optimize. A baseline with gradient would be trained to shrink the loss rather than to predict value.
reinforce_policy_loss.Masked mean over valid tokens: how do yo: Multiply by the mask, sum, and divide by mask.sum(). Use where rather than multiplying NaNs so masked positions add neither value nor gradient.
reinforce_policy_loss.What input validation matters here and w: Shapes must match and the mask must have at least one valid token. NaN spreads silently through training, so fail fast.
reinforce_policy_loss.Token-mean versus sequence-mean normaliz: Token-mean gives every token equal weight, so long responses dominate. Sequence-mean gives each response equal weight, so tokens in short responses weigh more.
reinforce_policy_loss.REINFORCE versus PPO: what does PPO add,: PPO adds clipped importance ratios for several update epochs and usually a critic. REINFORCE with a good baseline (RLOO) is enough for on-policy single-update training.

grpo_token_loss.Walk me through the GRPO objective end t: Policy: current log-probs. Old policy: the ratio for clipping. Reference: the KL term. Reward: group-relative advantages broadcast to tokens.
grpo_token_loss.Why is there no value network in GRPO, a: Group statistics replace the value network. The baseline comes from other samples of the same prompt.
grpo_token_loss.How do you broadcast a per-sequence adva: Unsqueeze the (B,) advantage to (B, 1) and let it broadcast over the (B, T) log-probs, then apply the mask.
grpo_token_loss.What denominator do you use for the loss: Per-sequence mean (original GRPO) versus total valid tokens (DAPO). Say which one makes each token's gradient depend on its response length.
grpo_token_loss.What is the role of beta, and what happe: beta weights the KL to the reference. Too large and the policy barely moves. Zero lets it drift, which risks hacking but is common for verifiable rewards.
grpo_token_loss.Sequence-level versus token-level loss a: DAPO uses token-level aggregation so long responses are not down-weighted per token and bad long patterns get penalized properly.
grpo_token_loss.What instability does GRPO show on long: Per-token ratios on long sequences get noisy and clipping becomes erratic, especially in MoE. GSPO uses a sequence-level ratio; DAPO uses clip-higher and dynamic sampling.

loss_aggregation_modes.In GRPO-style training, how can the way: The averaging decides how much each token and each response contributes. It creates length biases in what gets reinforced.
loss_aggregation_modes.What is the length bias that Dr. GRPO po: Dividing each response's loss by its own length means long wrong answers get less penalty per token, so wrong answers grow long.
loss_aggregation_modes.Write the four aggregation modes. For ea: With V valid sequences, n_b tokens in sequence b and padded length T: token-mean weighs each token 1/(sum of n), seq-mean-token-mean 1/(V * n_b), seq-mean-token-sum 1/V, seq-mean-token-sum-norm 1/(V * T). Compare n_b = 10 with n_b = 1000.
loss_aggregation_modes.Which sequences should take part in a se: Only sequences with at least one valid token. An all-masked sequence gives 0/0 and should be excluded from the denominator.
loss_aggregation_modes.Why can loss * mask still produce NaN, a: NaN or inf in masked positions times 0 is still NaN. Use torch.where or zero out the loss before multiplying.
loss_aggregation_modes.Token-mean versus sequence-mean: which o: Token-mean, or a constant normalizer, so long reasoning traces get per-token signal equal to short ones.
loss_aggregation_modes.How does the aggregation mode interact w: Token-mean must use the global token count across micro-batches and ranks. Averaging per micro-batch reweights them.

ppo_clipped_policy_loss.Why does PPO clip the importance ratio?: The ratio measures how far the new policy has moved from the rollout policy. Clipping removes the incentive to move beyond 1 +/- eps.
ppo_clipped_policy_loss.Why is the objective the minimum of the: The minimum is a pessimistic bound: it clips only when that would increase the objective, and still applies the full penalty when the ratio moves the wrong way.
ppo_clipped_policy_loss.Compute the ratio in log space. Why exp(: Ratios of tiny probabilities are unstable. Subtracting log-probs is exact and then exp once.
ppo_clipped_policy_loss.What is dual-clip, and which case does i: Dual-clip bounds the objective for negative advantages when the ratio is very large (above c, for example 3), to avoid huge penalties from stale data.
ppo_clipped_policy_loss.old_logprobs and advantages are constant: The gradient then flows into the rollout policy's log-probs or into the advantages, which changes the objective. Loss values can look fine while updates are wrong.
ppo_clipped_policy_loss.How do the number of PPO epochs and mini: More epochs and minibatches let the ratio drift further, so clipping activates more. Keep the total drift per rollout in mind.
ppo_clipped_policy_loss.What metric would you log to tell whethe: Clip fraction: the share of tokens where clipping is active. Values rising above about 0.2 to 0.3 suggest steps that are too large.

ppo_value_loss.What does the critic predict in PPO for: The expected return (value) at each response token, from a value head on the LM, used as the GAE baseline.
ppo_value_loss.Why clip the value update around old_val: It prevents the critic from changing too fast per update, like policy clipping, keeping it consistent with the data.
ppo_value_loss.Why take the maximum of clipped and uncl: Taking the max is pessimistic, like the policy's min. It keeps the larger error, so clipping never gives a smaller loss artificially.
ppo_value_loss.How do you mask and average the value lo: Mask to response tokens and average over valid ones. 0.5 makes the gradient of the squared error the plain error.
ppo_value_loss.What happens if returns are not detached: The critic target would move with the critic, and gradients would flow into the return computation.
ppo_value_loss.Value clipping has been reported to hurt: When returns change a lot between updates, or with reward scaling changes. Clipping then slows needed updates. Andrychowicz et al. found it can hurt.
ppo_value_loss.Why have GRPO-style methods dropped the: A critic costs memory and is hard to train on sparse terminal rewards. You lose per-token credit assignment and variance reduction.

gae_advantage.What is Generalized Advantage Estimation: A weighted sum of TD residuals. gamma is the discount; lambda interpolates between one-step TD (low variance, biased) and Monte Carlo (unbiased, high variance).
gae_advantage.What are the two extremes lambda = 0 and: lambda = 0: A_t = delta_t = r + gamma V(t+1) - V(t). lambda = 1: A_t = discounted return - V(t).
gae_advantage.Walk through the backward recursion for: delta_t = r_t + gamma V_{t+1} (1 - done) - V_t; A_t = delta_t + gamma lambda (1 - done) A_{t+1}. You need V at T for bootstrapping.
gae_advantage.How do dones enter both the TD residual: At a done there is no next state: zero the bootstrap in delta and stop the recursion so the next episode's advantage does not leak back.
gae_advantage.Why run the loop backwards over time but: Each A_t depends on A_{t+1}, so time must be sequential. Batch entries are independent and vectorize.
gae_advantage.For an LLM with one reward at the final: A_t = final reward - V_t for every token (with gamma = 1): Monte Carlo minus the baseline.
gae_advantage.How does critic quality affect GAE, and: GAE trusts V for bootstrapping. A biased critic injects systematic errors, while no critic (MC) is just noisier.

gspo_sequence_ratio.What is GSPO, and why does it replace PP: Group Sequence Policy Optimization. Rewards are per sequence, so importance weighting and clipping are done per sequence to match.
gspo_sequence_ratio.Why length-normalize the sequence log-ra: A sum of log-ratios grows with length. The length-normalized geometric mean keeps the ratio's scale comparable across lengths.
gspo_sequence_ratio.Why aggregate the log-ratio first and ex: The mean of log-ratios then exp gives the geometric mean, which is stable. Averaging raw ratios lets one outlier token dominate.
gspo_sequence_ratio.How do you handle a sequence whose mask: Define its log-ratio as 0 (ratio 1) or exclude it. Do not divide by zero.
gspo_sequence_ratio.What does this ratio look like for a seq: The same per-token drift gives the same normalized ratio at length 1 and at length 1000, while an unnormalized product would be astronomically different.
gspo_sequence_ratio.Why is sequence-level importance weighti: MoE routing changes between rollout and training, making per-token ratios very noisy. A sequence-level ratio averages that out.
gspo_sequence_ratio.What information is lost by collapsing p: Token-level credit: one bad token among many good ones cannot be singled out, and all tokens share one clip decision.

dapo_dynamic_sampling.What is DAPO's dynamic sampling, and why: Filter out groups whose rewards are all the same (all correct or all wrong) and resample until the batch is full. Such groups have zero advantage.
dapo_dynamic_sampling.Why must keep or drop decisions apply to: Advantages are defined relative to the group. Keeping part of a group changes its baseline and breaks the estimate.
dapo_dynamic_sampling.How do you compute the per-group spread: Per-group max minus min (or std) via reshape, compare with tol, then repeat_interleave the keep flag back to responses.
dapo_dynamic_sampling.What does tol protect against with conti: Floating rewards that differ by rounding noise would count as informative. tol treats near-identical rewards as equal.
dapo_dynamic_sampling.After filtering, the batch may be smalle: It generates more rollouts until enough informative groups accumulate, or trains on a smaller batch and rescales.
Worth it when many groups are degenerate, since the extra sampling replaces wasted compute. Wasteful when almost all groups already vary.
dapo_dynamic_sampling.How does the fraction of degenerate grou: As the model improves, more groups become all-correct. A rising fraction means the curriculum is too easy.

dapo_clip_higher_loss.What is Clip-Higher in DAPO, and why use: It uses a larger upper clip bound (for example 1.28) than the lower one (0.8), letting low-probability tokens with positive advantage grow more.
dapo_clip_higher_loss.How does clip-higher relate to entropy c: With symmetric clipping, unlikely tokens barely increase, so entropy collapses and exploration dies. Raising the upper bound keeps them viable.
dapo_clip_higher_loss.Walk through which tokens hit the upper: A > 0: clipped when the ratio exceeds 1 + eps_high. A < 0: clipped when the ratio drops below 1 - eps_low.
dapo_clip_higher_loss.Why detach both old log-probs and advant: Both come from rollout time and must be constants. Gradient through them corrupts the update.
dapo_clip_higher_loss.How do you reduce the per-token objectiv: Sum the objective over valid tokens and divide by the total valid token count (token-level mean), excluding padding.
dapo_clip_higher_loss.What risk does a larger upper clip bound: A bigger step for positive-advantage tokens can destabilize training. Tune by watching entropy and clip fractions.
dapo_clip_higher_loss.Compare clip-higher with adding an entro: Clip-higher targets the specific mechanism (rare tokens not growing). An entropy bonus raises randomness everywhere and can add noise.

vineppo_mc_value.What problem with learned critics does V: Learned critics for LLM reasoning are inaccurate, which gives poor credit assignment across reasoning steps.
vineppo_mc_value.How does Monte Carlo rollout from interm: From an intermediate state, sample K continuations with the current policy and average their final rewards as V(state).
vineppo_mc_value.Why average across the K continuations o: Each state needs its own value. Mixing continuations from different states blurs the per-step credit.
vineppo_mc_value.Why does the last state use the trajecto: At the end nothing is left to roll out, so its value is the realized terminal reward.
vineppo_mc_value.How does K trade estimation variance aga: Variance falls as 1/K while generation cost grows linearly with K.
When the critic is poor, as in math reasoning, and generation is cheap relative to the gains. Not when rollouts are very expensive.
vineppo_mc_value.What does VinePPO require from the envir: The ability to reset to any intermediate state and continue generating, which needs prefix caching or a resettable environment.

rollout_batch_assembly.What does a trainer need from a rollout: Padded ids, attention and response masks, old log-probs, per-token advantages and rewards, all aligned per token. A misalignment still trains, just on the wrong targets.
rollout_batch_assembly.Why broadcast one scalar advantage per r: The reward judges the whole response. Every token that produced it shares the credit (no critic), so the scalar is repeated across its tokens.
rollout_batch_assembly.How do you pad rows with different promp: Pad each row to the batch max. The mask is True on generated positions only: after the prompt length, before the total length.
rollout_batch_assembly.What should happen for a response that g: Keep the row with an all-False response mask so it contributes nothing, or drop it consistently from every tensor.
rollout_batch_assembly.Which tensors need which dtypes, and why: ids as long, masks as bool, log-probs and advantages as float32. Float masks in integer math or bfloat16 advantages silently change the loss.
rollout_batch_assembly.Padding every row to the batch max waste: Packing several sequences into one row (with cu_seqlens or a block-diagonal mask) or dynamic batching. It complicates masks, position ids and per-sequence reductions.
rollout_batch_assembly.Where would you add assertions in the pi: At assembly: equal lengths, mask sums equal to the generation lengths, advantages zero outside the mask, and log-prob positions aligned with target tokens.

verl_dataproto_filter_chunk.What is VERL's DataProto, and why carry: A batch container with a dict of tensors, a dict of non-tensor arrays (strings, ids) and meta info. Keeping them together means indexing keeps every field aligned.
verl_dataproto_filter_chunk.Why filter out rows with an empty respon: Rows with no response tokens add nothing to the loss, can produce 0/0 in means, and waste compute.
verl_dataproto_filter_chunk.Why use select_idxs rather than rebuildi: select_idxs slices every field (tensor and non-tensor) with the same indices, so no field is dropped or misaligned.
verl_dataproto_filter_chunk.Chunking requires the row count to divid: Pad with dummy rows and mask them, drop the remainder, or rebalance the chunks. Say what each does to the gradient.
verl_dataproto_filter_chunk.How do you keep the original order acros: Use index-based selection, which keeps relative order, and chunk contiguously. Order matters for grouping (GRPO groups) and for matching results back.
verl_dataproto_filter_chunk.Filtering changes the effective batch si: The effective batch size changes the gradient noise and the loss scale between steps. Normalize by the actual token count.
verl_dataproto_filter_chunk.What would you log at this boundary to d: Rows before and after filtering, tokens per rank, per-chunk sizes, the reason each row was filtered, and group integrity.

grpo_train_step.Walk me through one GRPO step from batch: Rollouts are generated and scored, and group advantages computed, before this step. In the step: policy log-probs, reference log-probs under no_grad, the loss (advantage-weighted log-probs minus beta times KL), backward and one optimizer step.
grpo_train_step.Which model is frozen, which receives gr: The reference is frozen (requires_grad False, eval mode, no_grad). The policy trains. Assert that the reference has no gradients after backward.
grpo_train_step.Where do you shift logits and input_ids: In a real trainer, logits[:, :-1] pair with input_ids[:, 1:], and the response mask shifts the same way. This exercise's batch is already aligned, so do not shift here.
grpo_train_step.Why compute reference log-probs under to: The reference never updates, so there is no need to store activations for backward. no_grad saves that memory.
grpo_train_step.Why must the returned metrics be detache: Metrics holding tensors with gradient keep the whole graph alive, which leaks memory across steps.
grpo_train_step.This step does one update per rollout. W: You need the old log-probs and clipped ratios, since later epochs are off-policy. Monitor KL and the clip fraction.
grpo_train_step.How would you scale this step to a model: FSDP or tensor parallelism for the policy, a separate inference engine for rollouts, and a sharded or offloaded reference.

agentic_rollout_loop.What is an agentic rollout, and how does: Generation over several turns with tool calls, where environment responses are part of the trajectory. Single-turn RL generates once and scores it.
agentic_rollout_loop.Which messages in the trajectory come fr: Policy: assistant messages and tool calls. Environment: tool results and observations.
agentic_rollout_loop.How do you execute tool calls and append: Parse the calls from the model output, run each tool, append a tool-role message with the result keyed to the call id, then call the model again.
agentic_rollout_loop.What happens when max_turns is reached b: Stop and return the trajectory as truncated. The reward decides how to treat an unfinished task.
agentic_rollout_loop.How do you handle an unknown tool name o: This exercise raises ValueError for an unknown tool name, since that is a harness bug. In production, a tool that raises usually becomes an error message for the model, so it can recover instead of the rollout crashing.
agentic_rollout_loop.Trajectory-level reward versus per-turn: One final reward cannot tell which turn helped. Per-turn rewards need a way to judge intermediate steps.
agentic_rollout_loop.Why do multi-turn rollouts make batching: Turns take different numbers of steps and tool latencies vary, so batches drain unevenly and GPUs idle waiting for tools.

agent_rollout_truncation.Why do multi-turn agent rollouts get tru: Trajectories must fit a fixed training context. Ignoring that crashes training or trains on misaligned partial data.
agent_rollout_truncation.Why do tool-output tokens get a False re: Tool outputs were not generated by the policy, so they are not actions and must not get policy gradient.
agent_rollout_truncation.How do you truncate ids, mask and rollou: Cut all three arrays at the same position so ids, mask and log-probs stay aligned.
agent_rollout_truncation.How does the overlong penalty change the: Subtract a penalty when the response was truncated, and apply it only to truncated samples.
agent_rollout_truncation.Why keep rollout-time log-probs at all,: They record the probabilities of the sampling policy, used for importance ratios or checks against trainer log-probs.
agent_rollout_truncation.Truncation penalty versus dropping trunc: A penalty teaches shorter responses but may punish correct long reasoning. Dropping them biases the data toward short responses.
agent_rollout_truncation.How does truncation interact with import: Truncation cuts tokens where rollout log-probs exist. Ratios must use the same token set, or the IS weights are computed on mismatched positions.

rl_eval_loop.What should an RL evaluation loop measur: Episode success, return and length under a fixed protocol. Training metrics are noisy and on-policy; evaluation is controlled and comparable.
rl_eval_loop.Why seed each episode with seed plus epi: Each episode then gets a different but reproducible start. The results are repeatable and not correlated with each other.
rl_eval_loop.How do you handle terminated versus trun: Terminated means a natural end; truncated means a time limit. Either way the episode is over, so stop stepping.
rl_eval_loop.Why call the policy exactly once per env: The environment's step and the policy's action must correspond one to one. Extra calls add randomness or cost.
rl_eval_loop.Which metrics are averaged per episode a: Return and success per episode; step-level stats such as action frequencies per step. Average in the right unit.
rl_eval_loop.Deterministic versus sampled actions dur: Deterministic shows the best-mode behavior; sampled matches training. Report which one and keep it consistent.
rl_eval_loop.How many episodes do you need before a s: Use a binomial confidence interval: the standard error is sqrt(p(1 - p)/n). Hundreds of episodes are needed for differences of a few percent.

pass_at_k.What does pass@k measure, and why is it: The probability that at least one of k samples is correct. Code and math have verifiers, and users can retry.
pass_at_k.Why is 1 - (1 - c / n) ** k a biased est: It treats the samples as independent draws with replacement using the plug-in rate c/n, and the nonlinear transform of that estimate is biased.
pass_at_k.Derive the unbiased estimator by countin: pass@k = 1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k): one minus the chance that a random size-k subset contains no correct sample.
pass_at_k.Why does evaluating C(n, k) directly fai: The binomials overflow or lose precision. Use the product of (1 - k/i) over i from n - c + 1 to n.
pass_at_k.What should the estimate be when fewer t: If n - c < k, every size-k subset contains a correct sample, so the estimate is 1.
pass_at_k.RL often raises pass@1 while pass@k at l: RL sharpens the distribution onto answers it already could find (better pass@1) but reduces diversity. It may not add new reasoning ability.
pass_at_k.pass@k versus majority voting versus a v: pass@k rewards coverage, majority voting rewards consistency, and verifier reranking rewards selection. Deployment usually matches pass@1 or reranking.

async_agent_rollout.Why run agent rollouts asynchronously, a: Tool calls and long generations leave GPUs idle. In synchronous mode the slowest trajectory in the batch sets the pace.
async_agent_rollout.What does bounded concurrency protect?: The inference server, tool APIs and memory: without a bound, you overload them and fail more.
async_agent_rollout.How do you bound concurrency with asynci: asyncio.Semaphore(n): acquire it around each rollout with async with.
async_agent_rollout.How do you apply a per-call timeout with: Wrap each call in asyncio.wait_for and catch TimeoutError per task, so one failure does not cancel the gather.
async_agent_rollout.How do you return results in input order: Remember each input index, and write each result into a preallocated list at that index.
async_agent_rollout.Timeouts turn slow samples into failures: Hard or long tasks time out more, so the training data over-represents easy, short trajectories.
async_agent_rollout.Async rollouts versus batched synchronou: Async keeps GPUs and tools busy but makes ordering and timing nondeterministic. Synchronous batching is reproducible but idles.

agent_env_adapter.What does an environment adapter do betw: It turns env observations into prompt tokens and model outputs into env actions, and records ids, masks and rewards in the trainer's format.
agent_env_adapter.Why must environment observations be exc: Observations come from the environment. Training on them teaches the model to predict the environment, not to act.
agent_env_adapter.How do you align token ids, mask and rew: Here response_ids hold only the policy's tokens, each masked True, and rewards has one entry per step. A full multi-turn sequence would also interleave the observation tokens, masked False.
agent_env_adapter.How do terminated, truncated and max_ste: Stop when the env terminates or truncates, or when you reach max_steps. Record which reason applied.
agent_env_adapter.How is the return computed and what happ: Sum the rewards up to and including the terminating step. Nothing after termination counts.
agent_env_adapter.Token-level versus step-level rewards in: Token-level rewards give fine credit but need token-level judgments. Step-level rewards match env semantics but credit whole actions.
agent_env_adapter.What goes wrong if the tokenizer re-enco: Re-encoding can produce different token ids than the policy sampled, so log-probs and ratios no longer match the actual actions.

slime_custom_generate_hook.What is Slime, and why does it expose a: An RL framework (SGLang plus Megatron). The hook lets you customize how samples are generated, for example multi-turn or tool use, without forking the framework.
slime_custom_generate_hook.How do finish reasons map to sample stat: stop maps to completed; length maps to truncated; abort maps to aborted. Each status tells the trainer how to use the sample.
slime_custom_generate_hook.Which sample fields must you update afte: tokens (prompt plus response), response_length, loss_mask, response text and status. Build a new tokens list because other code may still hold a reference to the prompt list.
slime_custom_generate_hook.What should the loss mask look like for: One value per generated token, typically all 1 for policy tokens, and 0 for tool or environment tokens.
slime_custom_generate_hook.How should an aborted generation be reco: Mark its status as aborted, so the trainer filters it out or requeues it rather than training on partial garbage.
slime_custom_generate_hook.Why should truncated samples usually sti: They still contain valid policy decisions. Training teaches that running long is costly, via a penalty or a separate status.
slime_custom_generate_hook.What are the risks of letting user code: User code can crash, hang or corrupt samples inside the hot path. Validate the outputs and apply timeouts.

rollout_train_boundary.What has to happen at the boundary betwe: Convert trajectories into aligned token tensors: ids, masks, per-token advantages, episode ids, and the log-probs from the rollout.
rollout_train_boundary.Why broadcast the trajectory return to e: With a single outcome reward, every policy token shares the credit (no critic).
rollout_train_boundary.Why zero advantages and loss mask on non: Environment and prompt tokens are not policy actions. Nonzero values would train on them.
rollout_train_boundary.Why keep episode ids after concatenation: Downstream steps such as group statistics, per-episode metrics and debugging need to know which tokens belong together.
rollout_train_boundary.Why not normalize advantages across epis: Normalization belongs where group structure is known and at a consistent scope. Doing it here can mix groups or double-normalize.
rollout_train_boundary.What does summing per-step rewards into: Which step caused success. All steps share credit, so good early steps in failed episodes get punished.
rollout_train_boundary.Where should advantage normalization liv: In one place in the algorithm (for example the advantage estimator) with an explicit scope, so it happens exactly once.

fully_async_rollout_buffer.What is fully asynchronous RL, and how d: Rollout and training run concurrently, and the trainer consumes data that may come from slightly older weights. Synchronous training alternates between the two.
fully_async_rollout_buffer.Why train as soon as a batch is ready in: It keeps the trainer busy and avoids waiting for the slowest rollout.
fully_async_rollout_buffer.How do you keep at most max_concurrency: A semaphore or a counter of in-flight tasks, refilled as tasks finish, with train_fn called whenever batch_size results are buffered.
fully_async_rollout_buffer.How do you preserve original order withi: Tag each result with its index and sort each batch by index before emitting it.
fully_async_rollout_buffer.What happens to timeouts and failures, a: Record timeouts and failures as dropped, not trained on. Flush the leftover items as a final smaller batch at the end.
fully_async_rollout_buffer.Async training makes data off-policy. Ho: Bounded staleness (for example one or two policy versions). Importance weighting or truncated IS corrects the mismatch.
fully_async_rollout_buffer.How do long-tail slow rollouts bias the: Short rollouts finish first and fill the batches, so long responses are under-represented and length behavior drifts.

rollout_weight_sync_staleness.Why do inference engine weights lag behi: Syncing weights to the inference engine takes time, and rollouts keep running during training, so the rollouts use older weights.
rollout_weight_sync_staleness.What is staleness, and why cap it?: The version gap between the policy that generated a sample and the current one. Large gaps make the data too off-policy.
rollout_weight_sync_staleness.How do you route complete, aborted and f: Complete samples within the staleness limit train, while stale and aborted ones go to retry because the prompt is still valid. Failed samples are dropped.
rollout_weight_sync_staleness.When is it safe to sync weights to the s: When no request is running on the old weights. Swapping mid-generation mixes two policies within one sample.
rollout_weight_sync_staleness.What should happen if lag is negative?: A sample from a newer version than the trainer means a bookkeeping bug. Raise an error rather than silently accepting it.
rollout_weight_sync_staleness.Strict on-policy versus bounded stalenes: Bounded staleness gives higher throughput and less idling but introduces an off-policy bias.
rollout_weight_sync_staleness.Besides dropping stale samples, how can: Weight each sample by pi_current / pi_behavior (truncated) so the gradient estimate stays nearly unbiased.

truncated_importance_sampling.Why do the rollout engine and the traine: Different kernels, precision, batch composition or quantization in vLLM versus the FSDP trainer give slightly different log-probs for the same token.
truncated_importance_sampling.What does importance sampling correct, a: It reweights samples from the rollout distribution to match the trainer's. Truncation bounds the variance from rare huge ratios.
truncated_importance_sampling.Write the token-level and sequence-level: Token: exp(train - rollout) per token, capped. Sequence: exp of the summed log-ratios, capped. Sequence is the true trajectory ratio but explodes and hits the cap much more often.
truncated_importance_sampling.Why must the weight be detached, and whe: It is a fixed correction factor, not something to optimize. It multiplies the per-token policy loss.
truncated_importance_sampling.How do you keep the weight finite when a: Clamp the log-ratio before exp and zero masked positions first, since padded garbage can overflow.
truncated_importance_sampling.How do you choose the cap? What do you m: Pick a small cap such as 2 and watch the fraction of capped tokens and the mean log-ratio. A spike means the engine is misbehaving.
truncated_importance_sampling.Truncated IS versus fixing the mismatch: Fixing the source gives exact on-policy data but costs speed. Truncated IS is cheap but biased and only patches small mismatches.

rl_data_audit.What integrity problems in an offline RL: Missing fields, duplicate ids and prompts, train/eval leakage, empty responses, label errors and format problems.
rl_data_audit.Why does train and eval ID overlap matte: Evaluation on training items overstates performance. The metric becomes memorization.
rl_data_audit.How do you report missing fields, duplic: Read the rows without changing them, collect findings in separate lists or counters, and return a report.
rl_data_audit.Why ignore empty IDs in duplicate and le: Empty ids are missing data, not a shared id. Counting them would create false duplicates.
rl_data_audit.What data structures keep this linear in: Hash sets and dicts from id to first index make one pass and O(1) lookups.
rl_data_audit.ID-based leakage detection misses paraph: Normalized-text hashing, MinHash or n-gram overlap, and embedding similarity with a threshold.
rl_data_audit.What is the cost of false positives in a: You discard good data or distrust valid results. Tune thresholds and review samples manually.

masked_perplexity.What does perplexity measure, and why co: exp of the average negative log-likelihood per token. Prompt tokens were given, not predicted.
masked_perplexity.Token-weighted across the batch versus m: Token-weighted pools all tokens, so long sequences dominate. The mean of per-sequence values weights sequences equally, and exp is nonlinear.
masked_perplexity.Why exponentiate the mean negative log-p: Averaging probabilities gives a different, non-geometric mean. Perplexity is the geometric mean of inverse probabilities.
masked_perplexity.What should happen with an all-zero mask: There are no tokens to average. Raise an error or return NaN explicitly rather than silently dividing by zero.
masked_perplexity.Why is perplexity a poor proxy for RL-tr: RL optimizes rewards, not likelihood of reference text. Better policies can have worse perplexity on a fixed corpus.
masked_perplexity.How can two models with the same perplex: Perplexity averages over all tokens. Accuracy depends on a few decisive tokens, formatting and calibration.

confidence_calibration.What is calibration, and why does it mat: Whether stated or implied confidence matches the actual accuracy. It matters for deciding when to trust or abstain.
confidence_calibration.How do accuracy, Brier score and ECE dif: Accuracy: fraction correct. Brier: mean squared error of the probabilities. ECE: the weighted average gap between confidence and accuracy per bin.
confidence_calibration.How do you assign confidences to equal-w: bin = min(floor(conf * B), B - 1), so 1.0 goes in the last bin. Check how 0 is handled.
confidence_calibration.Why weight each bin's gap by its count?: Bins with more samples should matter more. Otherwise a nearly empty bin could dominate.
confidence_calibration.How do empty bins affect ECE?: They have no samples and no gap. Skip them, with weight zero.
confidence_calibration.Why is ECE sensitive to the number of bi: Bin width trades bias against variance. Alternatives: adaptive or equal-mass bins, smooth calibration curves, and the Brier score.
confidence_calibration.RL with correctness rewards often makes: Reward calibrated confidence (proper scoring rules such as Brier), use temperature scaling, or add an abstain option.

embedding_diversity_selection.Why select diverse training data, and wh: Diverse data covers more of the task space and reduces redundancy. Embeddings capture semantic similarity.
embedding_diversity_selection.What is farthest-first traversal?: Pick a start point, then repeatedly add the point farthest from its nearest selected point. It is a 2-approximation for k-center.
embedding_diversity_selection.How do you maintain each row's distance: Keep min_dist per row. After each pick, update it with the minimum of the old value and the distance to the new pick. That is O(N) per step.
embedding_diversity_selection.Why cosine distance rather than Euclidea: Embedding direction carries meaning, while norms vary with length or frequency. Cosine ignores the norm.
embedding_diversity_selection.How do tie-breaking and the seed index a: Fix the first pick (the seed index) and break ties by lowest index, so the same input gives the same output.
embedding_diversity_selection.Diverse in embedding space does not mean: Quality, difficulty, label correctness and relevance to the target task. Combine diversity with a quality filter.
embedding_diversity_selection.Farthest-first tends to pick outliers. H: Filter outliers first, cap each point's distance, or use density-aware sampling.

gradient_orthogonality_audit.What does the cosine similarity between: Whether two examples push the parameters in similar (positive), unrelated (near zero) or opposing (negative) directions.
gradient_orthogonality_audit.What do negative cosines mean for multi-: The tasks conflict: improving one hurts the other, so the combined gradient cancels.
gradient_orthogonality_audit.How do you compute pairwise cosines for: Normalize the gradient rows to unit length, then G G^T gives all pairwise cosines.
gradient_orthogonality_audit.How do you count unordered off-diagonal: Take the upper triangle with triu_indices(N, N, offset=1) to count each unordered pair once.
gradient_orthogonality_audit.Why reject zero gradients?: A cosine with a zero vector is undefined (0/0), so the result is meaningless.
gradient_orthogonality_audit.How expensive are per-example gradients: One backward per example is O(N) passes. Approximations: random projections, last-layer gradients, LoRA gradients or per-sample gradient tricks.
gradient_orthogonality_audit.Gradient conflict methods such as PCGrad: When tasks consistently conflict, shown by negative cosines, and one task's gains hurt another. PCGrad removes the conflicting component.

masked_kd_kl.When training a small model or compressi: Logit distillation (KL to the teacher), sequence-level distillation on teacher outputs, feature matching and on-policy distillation. Pick one you know well.
masked_kd_kl.For sequence- or token-level knowledge d: Forward KL(teacher || student) is mass-covering: the student spreads over all teacher modes. Reverse KL is mode-seeking: the student commits to a few.
masked_kd_kl.Why divide the logits by a temperature T: T > 1 softens both distributions to expose the dark knowledge. The soft gradient scales as 1/T^2, so multiplying by T^2 keeps its magnitude.
masked_kd_kl.What goes wrong if padding or masked pos: Padded positions add fake targets and gradients. Use log_softmax for both, compute the KL per position, and take a masked mean.
masked_kd_kl.Should gradients flow back into the teac: No: the teacher is fixed. Compute teacher logits under torch.no_grad() or call detach().
masked_kd_kl.If every position in the batch is masked: With no valid positions, the mean is undefined. Raise an error for an empty mask and for T <= 0 rather than returning NaN.
masked_kd_kl.Temperature KD is teacher-forced distill: The student trains on teacher-forced prefixes but generates from its own. Errors compound. On-policy distillation addresses this.
masked_kd_kl.Compared with plain cross-entropy SFT on: The full distribution carries the teacher's uncertainty and near-miss answers (more signal per token). It costs teacher logits at train time, storage, and a shared vocabulary.

opd_sampled_kl_advantage.What is on-policy distillation, and how: The student samples its own outputs and the teacher scores them token by token. Teacher-forced KD trains on teacher or data prefixes the student may never produce.
opd_sampled_kl_advantage.Why evaluate the teacher on student-gene: The student then learns to fix the mistakes it actually makes, avoiding the train-test mismatch of teacher forcing.
opd_sampled_kl_advantage.Why is student minus teacher log-prob a: The expectation over student samples of log p_student - log p_teacher is exactly KL(student || teacher), so each sampled token gives an unbiased estimate.
opd_sampled_kl_advantage.Why must the shaped advantage be detache: It is a reward-like weight for the policy gradient. Gradient through it would optimize the estimate itself rather than the policy.
opd_sampled_kl_advantage.How do masked positions stay exactly zer: Multiply by the mask or use torch.where so padded positions are exactly 0 and add no gradient.
opd_sampled_kl_advantage.Sampled-token reverse KL versus full-voc: The sampled token is cheap and unbiased but noisy. The full vocabulary is exact with lower variance but needs all teacher logits.
opd_sampled_kl_advantage.How do you choose beta against the task: Balance the scales: the KL per token versus the reward magnitude. Tune on the validation reward and the distance to the teacher.

opsd_privileged_context_kl.What is on-policy self-distillation with: The same model acts as its own teacher by seeing extra information (such as the gold solution). The student version without it is trained toward the teacher's distribution.
opsd_privileged_context_kl.Why must the student generate without se: At test time there is no gold solution. Generating with it would teach behavior that depends on information the model will not have.
opsd_privileged_context_kl.Why call the same model twice on the sam: Both score the same student tokens: once without the privileged context (student) and once with it (teacher). That gives a per-token KL on identical actions.
opsd_privileged_context_kl.Which call should receive gradients, and: Only the student call. The privileged call is the target and must be detached, otherwise the model learns to change its teacher.
opsd_privileged_context_kl.How do you apply the mask and average th: Compute the KL per token, multiply by the mask, sum, and divide by the number of valid tokens.
opsd_privileged_context_kl.What leaks if privileged context reaches: The model learns to rely on the answer being present, and the evaluation becomes contaminated.
opsd_privileged_context_kl.How does self-distillation compare with: No second model is needed, and the teacher improves with the student. But the teacher is only as good as the model plus the hint.
